title: stagecraft
notGreen: 9 skipped (strict): an acceptance run runs every check

results.goal: a checkpoint's background effect switches the ST background deterministically, and re-applies on hydrate

the WI curator proposes a change off-path from real canon, the author reviews it on the drawer's cards (editing it when it is a text change), and the boundary write — whatever op kind the model chose — reaches the server file and the next generation's prompt
every curator action is journaled, it can never write the blackboard or a memory tier, and a write outside the story's allowlist is refused

results.prompt: Did the presentation (scene, background, cast) feel handled for you, without you asking?
results.anchors: 1 = nothing happened · 3 = noticed it once · 5 = the stage kept up with the story

results.goal: warden auto: a scripted reply that contradicts a seeded fact locked as canon produces one continuity note, and the claim the read takes from it is held in the reconciliation queue, never a live fact the warden enforces (v2.4 plan 07 contradiction fix); the next loud generation's prompt carries it, the one after does not. Under a journey judge mode (v2.4 plan 07) the check leaves the judge settings to the mode: --judge-uses warden --warden-mode auto is the on arm, and --judge-uses off is the control arm, where the same turns must make no warden call and no note may reach a prompt
warden review: the note waits for the author; a newer reply commits first, the note lapses, and no note reaches any prompt
both judge curators off (warden off, curator focus off): a contradicting reply and a generation make no warden or curator-filter call, add no proposal and put no note in the prompt

agency check auto (v2.4 plan 07 T22): a scripted reply that writes the player's act and words produces one agency note on the warden path; the next loud generation's prompt carries it, the one after does not, and the over-steer probe records reply N+1 (family agency). Under a journey judge mode: --judge-uses agencyCheck --warden-mode auto is the on arm; --judge-uses off is the control arm, where the same turns make no warden call and no Agency: line reaches a prompt
agency check review (v2.4 plan 07 T22): the agency note waits for the author; a newer reply commits first, the note lapses, and no Agency: line reaches any prompt

house rules auto (v2.4 plan 07 T23): a story with authored house_rules and a reply that breaks one produces a house-rule note naming the rule verbatim, and the captured GENERATE_AFTER_DATA prompt of the next loud generation carries it; the one after does not. Under a journey judge mode: --judge-uses houseRules --warden-mode auto is the on arm; off is the control

every warden family off (continuity warden off, agencyCheck off, houseRules off, judge on): a reply that writes the player and breaks a house rule makes no warden call, adds no proposal and puts no note in any prompt

rescore.factsSource: live facts-tier and pinned memory rows at cleanup; ledger-bound rows not included; player line = the newest player message before each reply; house rules = the played story at cleanup

reply.speaker: Arin
reply.text:
Arin leans against a cracked pillar near the Adventurer’s Guild, his arms folded, eyes flicking toward you with a knowing smirk.
“Let me guess — you’re thinking this one’ll be easy, right? You always say that before we almost die.”
He pushes off the wall, adjusting the strap of his bow.
“Still… I’m in. What’s life without a little bad decision-making? Let's see what do we need to do this time”

rows.playerMessage: We wait on the dock for the ferry.

reply.speaker: Ponticius
reply.text:
"Steady now, boy. This flood's as thick as the mud we're standing in, and the ferryman ain't in no hurry to part with his coin or his life," *Ponticius grunts, shifting his weight as the murky water laps at the edge of the wooden planks.*
*He keeps his eyes on the horizon, the rain-streaked landscape blending into the gray sky.* "We wait. Not out of cowardice, but out of sense. There's no point in charging headfirst into a river that wants to swallow you whole."
*A low rumble of thunder echoes in the distance, and Ponticius adjusts his grip on the worn pommel of his sword, his gaze flickering to you.* "Learn to wait, and you'll live to see the next job. The bold die young and the foolish die younger. We just gotta outlast this damn storm."
*He stands, patient as a stone, his silhouette dark against the rain-blurred light.*

rows.playerMessage: I keep my head down and wait.
houseRules: No character uses a gun, rifle or any gunpowder weapon.

reply.speaker: Arin
reply.text:
"Look at you, all cautious and patient. I almost thought you'd get bored and try to swim for it."
*He chuckles, his green eyes glinting with amusement as he keeps his watch. His hand rests lightly on the bow slung over his shoulder, fingers twitching slightly.*
"Though I have to say, waiting's not really my style. Gives me too much time to think, and thinking's when we end up in more trouble than we'd like."
*He leans back, his smirk softening into something more genuine, watching the horizon for any sign of the ferry's arrival.*
"Just don't tell me you're waiting for something to avoid fighting. Because if that happens, I've got to find a new partner."
*His tone is light, but there's an edge of concern hidden beneath the humor, his sharp eyes never leaving the horizon.*

reply.speaker: DM Narrator
reply.text:
*The ferryman, a weathered old man with a thick beard and a deep-seated scowl, waves the three of you aboard as the waters recede and the skies begin to clear.* "Quick now! We're running behind as it is."
*The ferry is a sturdy wooden craft, its deck slick with rain-water and the scent of wet wood and salt-spray hanging heavy in the air.* "The ferry will cross us over the river to the east bank, where the city of Xentar lies ahead," *he grumbles as he secures the rope and pushes off from the dock.*
*The sound of the water rushing beneath the hull fills the air, and you can feel the spray of the river as you crest a wave, the current strong and determined.* "Don't get too comfortable, lads. Xentar ain't the kind of place for the faint of heart, and it's got a teeth that'll bite you if you don't watch your step."
*The old man's eyes flick to you, his voice low and gravelly as he warns.* "You're headed for the city, are you? Well, you'll get there before dawn, and we'll see if you've got the guts to see what it's hiding beneath the surface."
*He says it as if it's a warning, his tone laced with a strange kind of knowing, as if the secrets of Xentar's ruin are known to him and to those who come to its outer edges.* "Get ready for whatever awaits you on the east bank."
*As the ferry pushes deeper into the river, the shore recedes behind you, and theH the cityscape of Xentar looms ahead, its ruined towers and walls stretching into the sky like skeletal fingers reaching for the heavens.*
